trajectory_summary: This is a short, well-paced verification call that moves cleanly through address, roof, title, utility, and bill before hitting a legitimate credit-score hard gate. The rep handled the DQ gracefully and briefly humanely, but missed two low-cost value-adds available in the same window: capturing the customer's self-offered six-month callback as a scheduled touch, and fully sitting with the divorce disclosure before moving to close.

observed_outcome.reasoning: The customer's stated credit score of 625 falls below the 670 threshold in qualifiers.credit_qualifier, and the rep explicitly says "I'll take you off the list for now" at 03:47 — a hard DQ with no appointment set, though the customer volunteered a future re-engagement window that was not converted into a scheduled callback.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Converting self-scheduled future interest into a locked callback
primary_coaching_focus.quote: I'll be looking for you in about six months after I get all this crap she that I inherited from her.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer did the hard part — naming a concrete re-engagement window — and the rep let it pass with only a soft, generic goodbye. This is the highest-leverage, lowest-cost fix on the call: capturing this line into an explicit callback date would turn a dead DQ into a live future pipeline entry.
